range.remark: Pss 87-90 complete. Ps 91 text begins pdf 137-138, verse notes -> next batch.

entries.emendation: supply an opening clause, e.g. מַה־טּוֹב מְעוֹן ה׳ or אַשְׁרֵי שֹׁכֵן מְעוֹן ה׳
entries.note: Before יסודתו בהררי קדש there is certainly a gap. Various fillers have been tried — Ewald's is nonsense; Olshausen's מה ידידה עיר אלהים does not fit, since עיר is feminine while the following יסדתו is masculine. Vielleicht מה טוב מעון ה', or אשרי שכן מעון ה' יסודתו וגו'.
מדבר בך is harsh; wohl a different reading is intended.
entries.flag: the proposed replacement is garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.emendation: הַאַזְכִּיר (interrogative); insert the divine name יָהּ, crowded out between לידעי and the next word
entries.note: אזכיר רהב ובבל is intelligible only as a question: leg. האזכיר, the interrogative ה absorbed by the following letters. הזכיר means 'praise, extol' (Isa 12:4, 62:6); רהב is Egypt, the storming sea. The divine name יה, originally present (should I extol these nations to those who know Yah?), was crowded out between the י of לידעי and the ה of the following word.

The hardest verse in the psalm, explicable only via Peshitta (וכל דאתמככו בכי = וכל מעני בך, 'all who are afflicted in thee'). ושרים is rendered 'singing' by Aquila and Symmachus (LXX omits it). For כחללים, Aquila has 'as with dances', Symmachus better 'as with flutes' — leg. כחלילים.
Not symmetrical with the psalm's own later usage; leg. שועתי, as at v.14.
נחשבתי is inexplicable; leg. נמשלתי, as Ps 143:7.

כמו חללים שכבי קבר should contain an intensification (beyond 'reckoned with the dead') that the received text doesn't convey. LXX add τραυματίαι καθεύδοντες, i.e. כמו חללים משלכים, recalling Isa 14:19 (ואתה השלכת מקברך) — 'thrown from the grave', unburied. Leg. accordingly כמו חללים משלכי קבר or מקבר.
Pesch. renders במצלות by 'in the shades of death', i.e. בצלמות.

entries.mt: עָלַי סָמְכָה חֲמָתֶךָ וְכָל־מִשְׁבָּרֶיךָ עִנִּיתָ סֶּלָה
entries.emendation: סָמְכָה → שֻׁפְּכָה (transposed letters); עִנִּיתָ → הֶעֱבַרְתָּ; סֶּלָה → עָלָי
entries.note: סמכה חמתך עלי is unintelligible; leg. by transposition שפכה 'poured out'. And וכל משבריך ענית סלה is wholly unintelligible — LXX 'all Thy waves Thou didst bring upon [me]', Pesch. similarly with no equivalent for סלה. Statt ענית leg. העברת (cf. Ps 42:8 משבריך עלי עברו), and statt סלה leg. עלי (confusion of ה/ע): the whole reading וכל משבריך העברת עלי.
דאבה cannot mean 'ache, hurt' here; Pesch. and Symmachus (ἐτάκη 'melted') point instead to a verb meaning 'flow' — either זבה or the Aramaic דבה.

entries.mt: עָנִי אֲנִי וְגֹוֵעַ מִנֹּעַר נָשָׂאתִי אֵמֶיךָ אָפוּנָה
entries.emendation: וְגֹוֵעַ → יָגֵעַ; מִנֹּעַר → מִכֶּלֶא; אֵמֶיךָ נָשָׂאתִי → אֶעֱנֶה(?); אָפוּנָה → אָפוּגָה
entries.note: וגוע would mean 'dying'; Pesch. and LXX ('in toils') point instead to a form of יגע/ינע 'weary'. מנער ('from youth') makes no sense; leg. מכלא 'from imprisonment' (cf. Ps 107:39, Isa 53:8). אמיך נשאתי is dark, since אימים is not secured in the plural and construes poorly with נשא; the versions render the phrase as a verb, suggesting אענה rather than אמיך, though נשאתי then remains unclear. And אפונה is untenable; leg. אפוגה (Michaelis), 'I grow numb'.
entries.flag: this crux is only partly resolved even by Graetz and is heavily garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: צמתתוני is redundant, too much; צתני would fully suffice.

entries.emendation: מַחְשָׁךְ → a verb form, חָשַׂכְתָּ (per Pesch.), or infinitive מֵחְשֹׁךְ (as v.10a)
entries.note: Readings vacillate between מהשך and מחשך (Rashi still read the latter); the transmitted form cannot be placed grammatically. Best is Pesch., which reads a verb ('Thou hast withheld from...'), or an infinitive parallel to v.10a.
LXX εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, i.e. לעולם, gives the most correct sense.

entries.mt: כִּי־אָמַרְתִּי עוֹלָם חֶסֶד יִבָּנֶה שָׁמַיִם תָּכִן אֱמוּנָתְךָ בָהֶם
entries.emendation: אָמַרְתִּי → אָמַרְתָּ (2nd person, God speaking); אֱמוּנָתְךָ → אֱמוּנָתִי; reorder to שָׁמַיִם תָּכִן בָּהֶם אֱמוּנָתִי
entries.note: LXX εἶπας: leg. אמרת — from here God's own speech begins. LXX/Pesch. render 'shall be established' for the heavens-clause: leg. congruently אמונתי statt אמונתך, since God is speaking; the ך was dittographed from the following ב (in בהם). The construction as transmitted is impossible, a kind of tmesis for the intended בשמים תכון אמונתי (Dyserinck emends similarly in part).
LXX μέγας καὶ φοβερός; leg. רב הוא ונורא.

entries.emendation: חֲסִין → חָסִיד; supply אִם before יָהּ
entries.note: חסין ('mighty') is out of place, since God's Huld — not His strength — is praised here; leg. instead a form of חסיד (cf. Jer 3:12, כי חסיד אני, used of God). Before יה LXX have εἰ, i.e. אם.
ידעי תרועה is unintelligible; leg. תעודה 'teaching, testimony' (cf. o. S. 154), perhaps also at Num 23:21 (leg. תעודת statt תרועת).
ירומו is not symmetrical with יגילון in the parallel half; leg. an equivalent verb of rejoicing there too.

entries.emendation: עֵזֶר → נֵזֶר ('crown'); שִׁוִּיתִי understood as שַׂתִּי, 'I have set'
entries.note: His translation ('Ich habe eine Krone auf einen Helden gelegt') shows he reads נזר 'crown' statt עזר 'help' (also Dyserinck).
entries.flag: exact letters of the OCR'd Hebrew proposal uncertain — verify at high res

entries.note: ישיא בו is unintelligible — deriving it from נשא 'lend' (so too LXX ὠφελήσει) is absurd; leg. ישאף בו 'shall snort/pant against him', the correct construction of the verb with ב.
Leg. אסיר statt אפיר (several interpreters).
ואתה זנחת leg. ועתה (cf. o. S. 116, 125, a recurring אתה/עתה confusion). And התעברת עם leg. על, Symmachus πρός, per the necessary construction.
נארת ברית cannot be said, since נאר/נער means 'shake off, overthrow'; leg. נבלת 'profaned'.
Passersby do not 'plunder' an unenclosed field, but trample it; leg. accordingly a verb of trampling rather than שסה 'plunder'.
entries.flag: the exact proposed verb is garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: Targum has 'backward' (לאחורא); leg. accordingly supply אחור: 'Thou hast turned back the edge of his sword'.
מטהרו is dark; vielleicht leg. עטרתו 'his crown' (in part per Krochmal).
ימי עלומיו as 'days of his youth' is senseless here; leg. שלומיו or שלותו 'his peace, tranquility'.
לנצח should be read with an interrogative ה prefixed, echoing the opening עד מה.
זכר leg. אדני, as v.51 (several interpreters). And מה חלד is unintelligible; the Syro-Hexapla's Symmachus points to מה חיי (cf. Ps 39:6).

entries.mt: זְכֹר אֲדֹנָי חֶרְפַּת עֲבָדֶיךָ שְׂאֵתִי בְחֵיקִי כָּל־רַבִּים עַמִּים
entries.emendation: עֲבָדֶיךָ → עַבְדֶּךָ (singular); בְחֵיקִי → בְּחַיַּי; כָּל־רַבִּים עַמִּים → כָּל דִּבַּת עַמִּים(?)
entries.note: חרפת עבדיך (plural) is incorrect; Pesch. has the singular עבדך. שאתי בחיקי is unintelligible; Pesch. has 'during my life' (בחיי). And כל רבים עמים is certainly incorrect, since in Hebrew the attributive adjective must follow its noun; Aquila read ἀδικίας = רעות, leg. instead רבות or more correctly רבה (cf. Ezek 36:6) — the whole phrase probably read שאתי בחיי כל דבת עמים 'the scorn of the peoples' (confusion of the endings ־ים/־ות).
Leg. מעוז 'stronghold' statt מעון 'dwelling' (cf. o. S. 428, his identical emendation elsewhere).

entries.emendation: keep אַתָּה אֵל together at the close of v.2 (against LXX, which draws אל into v.3 as a negation)
entries.note: LXX have only σὺ εἶ (=אתה) at the close of v.2, drawing אל into the next verse as the negative particle (אל תשב, 'return not'). Better: leg. אתה אל at the end of v.2 ('Thou art God'), which the unnegated form תשב in v.3 itself supports.

entries.mt: תָּשֵׁב אֱנוֹשׁ עַד־דַּכָּא וַתֹּאמֶר שׁוּבוּ בְנֵי־אָדָם
entries.emendation: עַד־דַּכָּא → עַד־דַּכְיוֹ (drawing the ו from ותאמר); וַתֹּאמֶר → וְתֹאמַר (future)
entries.note: Draw the ו of ותאמר back to form עד דכיו, and statt the perfect ותאמר leg. the future וְתֹאמַר, per Aquila's ἐρεῖς.

entries.mt: כִּי אֶלֶף שָׁנִים בְּעֵינֶיךָ כְּיוֹם אֶתְמוֹל כִּי יַעֲבֹר
entries.emendation: כִּי יַעֲבֹר → אֲשֶׁר עָבַר (the י of יעבר a dittograph)
entries.note: LXX 'yesterday', Pesch. 'that passed': leg. אשר עבר, the י of יעבר being dittographed, כי read as the relative אשר.

entries.mt: זְרַמְתָּם שֵׁנָה יִהְיוּ בַּבֹּקֶר כֶּחָצִיר יַחֲלֹף
entries.emendation: זְרַמְתָּם → זְרַמְתָּנוּ (or עַמְתָּנוּ); שֵׁנָה יִהְיוּ → שְׁנוֹת חַיֵּינוּ; delete the first בַּבֹּקֶר as dittograph (or read כַּיֶּרֶק)
entries.note: זרמתם is unclear as a verb, and its object is oddly third person when the psalm otherwise uses first-person plural throughout; leg. in any case זרמתנו (or, by letter-interchange, עמתנו). שנה ('sleep') cannot stand — what has sleep to do here? LXX 'years', Pesch. likewise: leg. שנים; but then יהיו is entirely unfitting — leg. שנות חיינו and delete the first בבקר as dittograph of the second (Hupfeld), or read כירק as at Ps 37:20: giving שנות חיינו כירק כחציר יחלף.

entries.mt: בַּבֹּקֶר יָצִיץ וְחָלָף לָעֶרֶב יְמוֹלֵל וְיָבֵשׁ
entries.emendation: וְחָלָף → corrupted, unresolved; יְמוֹלֵל → יִמַּל (the ל a dittograph)
entries.note: The morning/evening antithesis belongs properly to b.; hence וחלף here is unintelligible, clearly badly corrupted. ימולל should be read passively (de Wette) or, more correctly, יִמַּל — the ל being a dittograph.
עלמנו is inexplicable as usually pointed; Symmachus κρύφια ('hidden things') points to עלומנו.

entries.emendation: הֶגֶה → a Hebraized Persian word for 'spider/spider-web'
entries.note: הגה ('sound, thought, sigh') fits nothing here. LXX offer two translations, 'like a spider(-web)' and 'meditation' (from הגי); Pesch. likewise 'like a spider-web', a Persian loanword also found in the Talmud (Sanhedrin 99b, Sukkah 52a), rightly explained by Rashi as 'spider'. הגה is thus the Hebraized form of this Persian word.

entries.mt: יְמֵי־שְׁנוֹתֵינוּ בָהֶם שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה וְאִם בִּגְבוּרֹת שְׁמוֹנִים שָׁנָה
entries.note: ימי שנותינו בהם yields no intelligible sense; leg. בחיים 'in life'. And בגבורות ('with strength'?) is likewise inexplicable, a makeshift rendering; leg. ואם בן גבורות, 'a son of strength, a vigorous one' (cf. idioms like בני חלוף, בני תמותה).

entries.mt: וְרָהְבָּם עָמָל וָאָוֶן כִּי־גָז חִישׁ וַנָּעֻפָה
entries.note: רהבם is more Aramaic than Hebrew — in Hebrew it means only 'the storming sea', but in Syriac 'restless, hasty activity'; עמל ואון is roughly 'trouble and hastiness'. But כי גז חיש ונעפה is extraordinarily dark, and the ancient versions' readings diverge sharply. A plausible reconstruction combining the variants is 'כי גז חיש מעלינו' — 'for it passes quickly away from us' — the predicate referring back to ימי שנותינו.
entries.flag: among the most heavily disputed cruxes in the psalm; the versional evidence is badly garbled in OCR — verify at high res before using

entries.note: וכיראתך עברתך is dark and surely corrupt. Vielleicht leg. ואך יראיך statt וכיראתך (cf. his note at Ps 119:38), then supply ישיבו, since the half-verse is otherwise too short: 'ואך יראיך ישיבו עברתך' — 'only those who fear Thee can turn back Thy wrath'.

entries.mt: לִמְנוֹת יָמֵינוּ כֵּן הוֹדַע וְנָבִא לְבַב חָכְמָה
entries.emendation: לִמְנוֹת → לְמַלְאוֹת; וְנָבִא → נָבִיא (drop the waw); reconstruct כֵּן הוֹדִיעָנוּ נָבִיא לְבַב חָכְמָה
entries.note: As transmitted the verse is wholly unintelligible. Given the frequent confusion of מ/ל, especially between the verbs מנה and מלא, it yields sense as למלאות ימינו 'to complete our days'. Targum and Talmud (Bava Batra 12a) already read נביא here as 'prophet'; the close should read כן הודיענו נביא לבב חכמה — 'so has a prophet of a wise heart made known to us' — referring to Deutero-Isaiah's promise of long life after the exile (Isa 65:20, 22), whose non-fulfillment the psalmist here laments.

The repetition of ומעשה ידינו כוננהו, missing in most LXX manuscripts, is perhaps a marginal variant that entered the text; in any case leg. כוננהו statt כוננה — it cannot be a liturgical refrain, since this psalm hardly served liturgical use.
